title: Invertibility of the closed affine coefficient mate
statement: In the finite dualizing coefficient setting, for l ≠ p and n ≤ m, an affine closed immersion i:Y→A^r over Spec(k) has an invertible counit-defined closed coefficient mate at the m-level dualizing complex.

source.place: paragraph 3, closed-chart descent and the ordinary counit-defined mate

proof.text: Apply coefficientDualizingClosedDescent at the affine chart and unpack its witness, including the isomorphism b and its counit equation.
Use the proper direct-image adjunction Hom equivalence to identify closedDualizingCoefficientMate with b by their counit equations, then transport IsIso b.

theorem closed_mate_isIso_aux (hl : l ≠ D.p) {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m)
    (r : ℕ) (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y]
    (aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of D.k))
    [IsSeparated aY] [LocallyOfFiniteType aY] [QuasiCompact aY]
    (i : Y ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin r)) (Spec (.of D.k)))
    [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hi : i ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin r)) (Spec (.of D.k)) ↘
      Spec (.of D.k)) = aY)
    [IsNoetherian Y]
    [IsNoetherian (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin r)) (Spec (.of D.k)))] :
    IsIso (Etale.closedDualizingCoefficientMate (finiteDualizingQuotient l E h) i
      (Etale.dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (finiteDualizingCoeff l E m))
        (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin r)) (Spec (.of D.k)) ↘ Spec (.of D.k))))
